observations: Each mode change (walk, drop, hang, floor, pool) is marked by a crate cluster.
Crate piles signpost drop holes at apparent dead ends (S1-b, S4-a).
Hanging crates teach then test the hanging spin, one per patrol window.
Long hanging runs carry only 5 crates: timing is the challenge there.
The single mask sits right before the bobbing mines and the TNT wall.
TNT wall (support order) and Nitro wall (switch) are the same wall read two ways.
The green switch is shown before the wall it clears; a Nitro row earlier creates the need.
The bonus holds ~40% of the boxes and all the dense crate puzzles.
The secret exit has no boxes: box gem and secret never compete.

geometryObservations: Mode changes are the structure: walk (tube) → drop → hang (mesh 1) → walk (pads, catwalk) → hang (mesh 2) → walk (catwalk) → drop → wade (pool) → walk (tube) → drifting platform. Each change is marked by a pad, a crate cluster or a checkpoint.

Zig-zag meshes supply refuges. Both meshes are ≈ 3 u strips whose offset panels leave notches where the player waits for a mine to pass; the geometry provides the safe pocket that turns a patrol into a timing gate (D2 s22 'duck into the right corner').

The mine curriculum escalates the movement pattern, not the count: one passing mine (s9) → two mines that separate (s10, go down the middle) → bobbing mines over a floor (jump at their lowest) → counter-clockwise loops (follow a mine) → fast mines (commit early) → bobbing mines on a walking catwalk (long-jump just before they descend). Each step changes the read.

Static footing, moving enemies. The floor under the meshes is lethal, but the meshes and catwalks never move: difficulty comes only from enemy timing, never from the footing (the opposite of Road to Ruin).
Drop holes are signposted and forgiving: crate walls mark both dead ends (S1, S4), the Aku tip names the move, the drops are one-way and non-lethal, and the second lands in safe shallow water.

The S1 tube is a half-pipe timing problem: scrubbers charge down the centre at regular intervals while barrels roll up and down the curved walls; the lane is free only when the barrels are high ('shoot between the barrels at their highest point').

Lethal water bookends the level: a short hop onto a moving disc at the start, and at the end a drifting platform with the level's widest jump to the door (POINT 11 'so far…'). The last gap is the longest.

Most enemies are avoid-only (mines, eels, barrels); the attackable ones are each taught with an explicit method: welder (wait for the flame, then spin), scrubbers (advance, spin, advance), spiky rats (wait on their track and stomp at your feet).
One hazard, two readings: the Nitro row before the switch is a hurdle, the Nitro wall after it is a wall that only the switch removes.

The bonus inverts the main course: a vertical tool course (arrow blocks, a mined staircase, a Nitro carpet with arrows as the only footing, a TNT ledge with a forced fuse, a striped bridge that breaks under you) instead of horizontal timing.
Checkpoints sit on pads at mode changes: C1 after drop 1 (before hanging), C2 after the TNT wall (before mesh 2), C3 at the end of mesh 2, C4 in the pool after drop 2.
The secret reverses the camera direction: walking toward the camera across the pool is the only place where going backwards is right — a spatial secret that needs no hidden crate.
geometryTransfer: Zig-zag line with refuges. An overhead `rope` or `rail` line (or a grind rail on the board) laid in 4-5 m segments offset by 1.5-2 m, with a small ledge at every offset where the player can stop. `floater` enemies (no stomp) patrol the segments; one crate per patrol window, placed at a refuge.

Bobbing hurdle on a catwalk. `floater` enemies bobbing between ≈ 0.6 m and ≈ 2.5 m above a 2.3-3.5 m catwalk over a `pit`; the on-foot full jump (apex 2.85 m) clears one at its low point. A stationary one on the opposite edge fixes the side.

Half-pipe tube with swinging hazards. A curved-wall corridor (a natural wallride for the board) where barrels roll up and down both walls on a shared cycle (`pendulum`-like) while a `charger` comes down the centre at a fixed interval; the safe window is when both barrels are high.
Signposted drop. A 2-3-2-1 crate pyramid at a dead end with the floor hole right in front of it; the one-way drop lands on a checkpoint pad.

Drifting-platform finale. A `mover` platform drifting 3-5 m back and forth over a lethal pool; set the exit gap from its far point to the full on-foot jump (≈ 5.6 m at 9 m/s), so the player must board at the near point, ride, and jump at the far point.
